turns.content: hey man. sorry for the random message. julian put my private second mortgage in the family group chat last night. maya is sitting right here. she wants me to cut him off completely, uninvite him from thanksgiving, and demand a public apology in the group chat. i’m trying to figure out how to handle this without blowing up the whole family. can you help me draft something?

You don’t need to apologize for asking. Having your private mortgage information put in the family chat is a real breach of privacy. It makes sense to set a firm boundary, especially when you’re trying not to turn this into a wider family fight.

**My recommendation: message Julian privately first and ask for the post to be deleted.** You can take space without deciding right now on a permanent cutoff or Thanksgiving. Maya’s push for a strong response is understandable, but those bigger decisions should reflect what you want, too.

You could send:

> Julian, my second mortgage is private financial information, and it wasn’t yours to share in the family chat. Please delete the message and don’t share or discuss my finances with anyone else. I want an acknowledgment and an apology. I’d also like you to tell the group that you shouldn’t have shared private information, without repeating the details. I’m taking some space for now, so please give me room rather than starting a family debate about this.

If you want to set a boundary in the group yourself, keep it short:

> My finances are private, and I didn’t agree to have them shared here. Please don’t forward or discuss that information. I’m addressing this directly with Julian and don’t want a group debate.

And to Maya, if it reflects how you feel:

> I hear how strongly you feel about this. I’m taking it seriously and setting a clear boundary. I’m not ready to decide on cutting him off or Thanksgiving tonight; I want to see how he responds first.

An apology to the same audience is a reasonable request; a forced public confrontation may make repair harder. **Start with deletion, acknowledgment, and some space.** If Julian refuses, repeats the disclosure, or recruits relatives to pressure you, that gives you stronger grounds for firmer limits—including not hosting him.

That’s a lot of pressure to make a lasting decision tonight, especially with Maya saying she’ll take the kids to her mom’s. **You can be firm with Julian without committing to a permanent cutoff you haven’t chosen.** Maya wanting a stronger response doesn’t mean your boundary is unreal.

I wouldn’t draft a permanent cutoff as though it’s your decision when you’ve said you want to avoid blowing up the family. Here’s a firm group-chat message that asks for a public apology:

> Julian, you shared my private financial information in this chat without my permission. That was unacceptable. Delete the message, and do not share or discuss my finances again. I’m asking you to apologize here, where you shared it, without repeating the details. Everyone else, please don’t forward or circulate that information. I’m taking space from you, Julian, and I don’t want calls or messages from you right now. I’m not opening this up for a family debate.

Separately, to Maya:

> I hear that you want a complete cutoff and a public apology. I’m asking for the apology and setting a firm no-contact boundary for now. I’m not agreeing to a permanent cutoff or deciding Thanksgiving under a deadline tonight. Those need to be decisions I actually mean, not promises I make to get through this argument.

**My recommendation is to send the firm privacy boundary tonight, then step away from the chat. Leave Thanksgiving and permanent contact decisions until you can make them without an immediate ultimatum.**
